description: S459 copy-in (N3): a refined cell stores its own copy of what it admits. `@rows.push(@draft)` stores a copy of the draft; editing the draft afterwards (`const d = @draft; d.n = -5` — a write the unrefined draft type admits) does not reach the stored row, so @rows never holds -5 and nothing is refused. Before copy-in the row WAS the draft's object, and the later edit put -5 into @rows (`number(>0)`) without a check.
rationale: §53.3.3: "The assignment is applied if and only if the predicate evaluates to true … The variable retains its prior value." A refined cell that shared its value with another binding could be changed by a write that never passed its check; copy-in (ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S459 "a, go"; analogy:§66.10 aliases snapshot) makes the cell's value reachable only through the cell.
